verdicts.reason: A just squeezes the centred stack into the strip. The one-line headline runs almost edge to edge with about 15px side margins, the subline and CTA are packed tightly underneath, and the bottom margin is thin, so it reads like a compressed copy of the original rather than a real banner. B rearranges the design to read left to right, which suits the shape, and gives the headline strong hierarchy. However, the subline is squeezed into an awkward 4-line centred column with orphan-like breaks ('Now in four / flavours.'), the gutter between 'sunshine.' and the CTA is very tight, and the right margin is cramped.
